name: BĂO HUÁNG
description: Băo Huáng (literally 'Protect the Emperor') is a high-stakes, asymmetric climbing game from the Shandong province of China. Played by exactly five players with a massive 168-card deck, the game is a unique blend of card shedding and social deduction. Two 'Royals' (The Emperor and the hidden Eunuch) must clear their hands before the three 'Commoners' can stop them. The heart of the game lies in the Eunuch's hidden identity, requiring the Commoners to observe card play closely to deduce who is the traitor in their midst.

content.text: Băo Huáng (literally 'Protect the Emperor') is a high-stakes, asymmetric climbing game from the Shandong province of China. Played by exactly five players with a massive 168-card deck, the game is a unique blend of card shedding and social deduction. Two 'Royals' (The Emperor and the hidden Eunuch) must clear their hands before the three 'Commoners' can stop them. The heart of the game lies in the Eunuch's hidden identity, requiring the Commoners to observe card play closely to deduce who is the traitor in their midst.

Bao Huang emerged from the coastal cities of Shandong (specifically Qingdao and Weifang) in the mid-20th century. It traces its ancestry to simpler climbing games like 'Zheng Fen' but introduced the imperial theme and the unusually large deck to accommodate longer, more strategic social sessions.
5 players. Team A: Emperor & Eunuch. Team B: Three Commoners.

168 cards. Take four standard 52-card decks, remove all 3s, 4s, and 5s. Use 4 Red Jokers and 4 Black Jokers. One specific Red Joker is marked 'Emperor' and one specific Black Joker is marked 'Eunuch'.
Players draw cards one by one from a shuffled wall. Everyone receives 33 or 34 cards.

items.text: Big Emperor (216 cards): Uses four full decks including 3s, 4s, and 5s. Much longer game time.
